motivating_question: If elapsed time is not treated as a causal antiviral agent, what accounts for falling viral load or loss of infectivity?

epistemic_boundary.claim: Elapsed time is not itself a molecular or cellular antiviral mechanism. Changes in viral load and infectivity arise from biological and physicochemical state transitions whose evolution can be indexed by time.
epistemic_boundary.do_not_promote: The statement that time does not exist is not recorded as an established scientific fact.

method: collect candidate mechanisms and source records
falsify the claim that waiting alone guarantees eradication
separate causal mechanisms from time-indexed rates
preserve latency and persistence as counterexamples

mechanism_classes: adaptive immune response including antibodies and cytotoxic lymphocytes
removal or turnover of infected cells
physiological clearance and loss of infectivity of free viral particles

dynamical_interpretation.core_balance: viral production and spread compete with neutralization, infected-cell removal, free-particle clearance and loss of infectivity
dynamical_interpretation.time_role: time indexes the evolution of these competing processes; it is not itself an antiviral effector
dynamical_interpretation.stronger_statement: Waiting does not guarantee clearance because persistent or latent infection can remain stable or reactivate.
